# Fagus sylvatica

_**Fagus sylvatica**_, the **European beech** or **common beech**, is a large [deciduous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deciduous "Deciduous") tree in the [beech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fagaceae "Fagaceae") family with smooth silvery-grey bark, large leaf area, and a short trunk with low branches.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fagus_sylvatica#cite_note-3) It is native to much of Europe, growing in humid climates.

## Description

_Fagus sylvatica_ is a large [tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree "Tree"), capable of reaching heights of up to 50 metres (160 feet) tall[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fagus_sylvatica#cite_note-4) and 3m (10ft) trunk diameter, though more typically 25–35m (82–115ft) tall and up to 1.5m (5ft) trunk diameter. A 10-year-old sapling will stand about 4m (13ft) tall. Undisturbed, the European beech has a lifespan of 300 years; one tree at the Valle Cervara site was more than 500 years old, the oldest known in the northern hemisphere.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fagus_sylvatica#cite_note-5) In cultivated forest stands trees are normally harvested at 80–120 years of age.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fagus_sylvatica#cite_note-6) 30 years are needed to attain full maturity (as compared to 40 for [American beech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fagus_grandifolia "Fagus grandifolia")). Like most trees, its form depends on the location; in forest areas, _F.sylvatica_ grows to over 30m (98ft), with branches being high up on the trunk. In open locations, it will become much shorter (typically 20m (66ft)) but more massive with a broader crown and stouter trunk.
